headings.text: A fresh client is not empty
Data Packages: pulling what the server holds

blocks.html:
⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. The opendefense-platform is under breaking development; verify against the code before relying on details.

This page covers what an end user can do on the device itself — no admin access, no kubectl, no Marti credentials — to get data into ATAK: the Import Tool for ad-hoc files and network links, and the Data Packages tool for pulling anything an integrator has published to the server. Read it even if you never touch a tablet: every action here has a server API twin (the subject of Publishing a data source programmatically), and watching what the UI does is the fastest way to understand what those API calls do to a client.

A fresh client is not empty

The enrollment zip (see Enrolling — getting a client certificate) is itself a data package: alongside server.pref and the client .p12 it carries the standard map sources — MML_Peruskartta.xml, MML_Ortoilmakuva.xml, Google_Roadmap/Hybrid/Satellite.xml — so a just-enrolled ATAK already has the Maanmittauslaitos base maps. On the first TLS connect the server's Default-ATAK device profile additionally pushes ATAK-default-settings.zip and the team-member toolbar automatically. One detail worth knowing: server.pref sets eud_api_sync_mapsources=false — the map list is baked into the package, not synced live from the server. How those defaults are defined and extended platform-side is the subject of Defining standard data sources.

The Import Tool: ad-hoc, on-device

blocks.alt: ATAK Import Tool — Select Import Type dialog

blocks.html:
The Import Tool (Import in the toolbox) offers three paths:

  • [Local SD] — a file browser over local storage. Pick the file, then a strategy: Copy (source file stays where it is) or Move. This is the same path the enrollment zip goes through, and it accepts anything ATAK has an importer for — KML/KMZ, GPX, GeoTIFF, data-package zips, map-source XMLs, .pref files.
  • [KML Link] — a network KML URL plus a refresh interval. The result lands under Remote Resources in Overlay Manager and re-fetches on the interval — the only self-updating feed an end user can set up without any server-side help.
  • [HTTP URL] — a one-shot fetch of any other importable file over HTTP.

Import is type-sniffed, and the resulting category matters more than you'd expect: a KMZ that is a GroundOverlay raster lands under GRG (georeferenced graphics), a vector KMZ under overlays — and a KMZ mixing both gets its rasters mosaicked and its placemarks silently dropped. Those rendering rules, learned the hard way, are the subject of Making your data render natively in ATAK.

Data Packages: pulling what the server holds

blocks.alt: Data Packages — Available Packages listing dronewx from the server

blocks.html: The Data Packages tool is how a user receives anything an integrator has published. Tap the download icon → pick the server → the Available Packages list (TAK calls this store Enterprise Sync) → select → Download. Every file uploaded via /Marti/sync/missionupload appears here for all users (Tool: public) — no mission subscription required.

blocks.code:
flowchart LR integ["Integrator
upload.sh / Marti REST"] sync["Enterprise Sync store
(dedupes by sha256)"] dp["ATAK Data Packages
Available Packages"] om["Overlay Manager
atak/overlays + atak/grg"] integ -->|"POST /Marti/sync/missionupload"| sync dp -->|"download icon → pick server → list"| sync sync -->|"Download → import per MANIFEST/manifest.xml"| om

blocks.html: Download imports the package per its MANIFEST/manifest.xml (onReceiveImport=true means no further prompts). From The drone weather demonstrator (scripts/dronewx, branch feat/dronewx-demo): cells.kmz and routewx.kmz land as atak/overlays/…, the gust rasters as atak/grg/…. The server-side twin is three Marti calls:

PUT  /Marti/api/missions/dronewx?creatorUid=...&defaultRole=MISSION_SUBSCRIBER
POST /Marti/sync/missionupload?hash=<sha256>&filename=...   # multipart, field: assetfile
PUT  /Marti/api/missions/dronewx/contents                   # {"hashes":["<sha256>"]}

Be candid with your integrator when it goes wrong: a raw KMZ uploaded without a manifest gets unzipped file-by-file on download, and ATAK asks the user to hand-place every PNG ("Select a location on the map to place: h00.png"). The fix is server-side — wrap content in a proper Mission Package — never something the user can work around on the device.

Sharing works the other way too: select a local package and SEND to push it to teammates via the server.

Toggling layers

Each imported KMZ is its own layer. The package contents panel and Overlay Manager both show eye icons per entry — from the demonstrator, the four gust rasters (+00h/+03h/+06h/+12h) toggle individually. One behaviour to internalize: with overlapping vector fills, the topmost fill wins the tap — to tap a route corridor lying under the weather cells, hide the cells layer first.
